status: AI-assisted draft, revised after three-agent challenge round and author answers; awaiting author sign-off
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft from the MAOO3 code and the author's design decisions (see write-up)
scope: Simplified zombie outbreak ABM for studying how similarity-based likeability changes human survival. Lab, medicine, births/aging, weapons, armor, learn and zombie rot are out of scope.
source_code_note: line numbers refer to simulation.py / zombie_storage.py, copied unchanged from MAOO3

competency_questions.question: Which attributes decide fight or flee?
What decides whether a bite infects, and how does that change after surviving one?
How do two humans become friends or rivals?
What does a human do with no zombie in sight, awake and asleep?
competency_questions.note: awake: walks toward a liked friend, otherwise wanders; asleep: stays put; lab research is out of scope

competency_questions.question: What happens to relationships when an agent turns or dies?
What is measured to show emergence, and against what baseline?

Human.description: A living person who can fight, flee, sleep, be bitten, form relationships and turn into a zombie.

aggression.meaning: percent chance to fight instead of flee when a zombie is in sight

susceptibility.meaning: percent chance that a bite infects

Zombie.description: A turned or initial zombie. Always chases the nearest living human. Has no relationships.
Zombie.note: Turning keeps the same object, agent_id and every attribute; only type, state, speed and slots change (simulation.py:505-509). Ids are humans 1..750 then zombies 751..1000 (zombie_storage.py new_state). Fields aggression, intelligence and susceptibility are retained but unused after turning.

Likes.capacity_rule: Each human holds at most 5 relationships, ranked by absolute value. Pairs not held are tracked in a transient per-direction pending table (not a relationship, never shown in the UI). In R8 all new values are computed from the tick-start values (snapshot). The candidates (held plus pending) are then ranked by |value| descending. Ties: a held pair beats a pending pair, then the lower partner agent_id. The top 5 are held, the rest stay pending. Entries with |value| < prune_below are dropped. A held slot is lost only by being outranked, by falling below prune_below, or by R10.
Likes.ends_when: either agent turns, becomes infected, or dies (author decision: a bitten friend is no longer a social partner)
Likes.symmetric_note: A->B and B->A are computed independently; compat is symmetric, slot contents may differ.

attack_scale.meaning: damage per step = strength * attack_scale * dt, both sides

like_rate.status: proposed, tune in a test run

like_decay.meaning: fraction of likeability lost per tick when the pair is apart
like_decay.status: proposed, tune in a test run

compat_slope.meaning: average random pair (d about 1/3) is neutral

pull_threshold.meaning: minimum likeability for an agent to walk toward a friend

cluster_threshold.meaning: likeability needed for two agents to count as one cluster, measurement only

prune_below.meaning: pending or held |L| below this is dropped

stop_distance.meaning: friend pull stops at or below this distance; above collision radius 12, below bond radius 40

turn_rate.meaning: wander heading change per unit time: heading += uniform(-turn_rate, turn_rate)*dt

run_ticks.meaning: no fixed length: each run continues until no living humans remain (author decision)

safety_cap_ticks.meaning: engineering guard only, in case zombies never reach the last humans; a run that hits it is reported as capped, not extinct

checkpoint_ticks.meaning: ticks at which survival is reported

cluster_sample_tick.meaning: tick at which cluster metrics are taken (also reported at 30 and 100)

outcome_window.meaning: ticks after the sample tick over which member loss is counted

rules.name: sleep
rules.text: At night humans do not move or decide. Zombies stay active. is_night uses the tick value before the end-of-tick increment.

rules.name: zombie behavior
rules.text: A zombie moves toward the nearest living human within the perception radius, otherwise wanders (R11).

rules.name: fight or flee
rules.text: Each tick, a human who sees a zombie fights with probability aggression/100, otherwise flees. A fighter moves toward the zombie, a fleer moves away.

rules.name: contact damage
rules.text: Contact damage is human-zombie only. In every step, for each pair (human, zombie) that are both alive at the start of the step and within the collision radius: the human loses zombie.strength*attack_scale*dt and the zombie loses human.strength*attack_scale*dt. Damage is summed over all touching partners and applied simultaneously at the end of the step; life is clamped at 0 and life <= 0 means dead (a creature killed this step still lands its hit). No human-human or zombie-zombie damage. Healthy, exposed, infected and sleeping humans take and deal damage. Stance changes movement only.

rules.name: bite
rules.text: After the 10th step of a tick, using positions after that step, each living human with state healthy or exposed that is within the collision radius of a living zombie rolls once, uniform(0,100). If roll < susceptibility it becomes infected (status_timer = 0), otherwise exposed (status_timer = 0, bites_survived + 1, susceptibility - susceptibility_decay, minimum 0). Infected humans are not bitten again. An exposed human can be bitten again, and a bite resets status_timer.

rules.name: infection progress
rules.text: Infected humans turn into zombies after turn_ticks. Exposed humans return to healthy after exposed_ticks. Timer semantics: a bite at the end of tick T sets timer 0 and R6 runs in the same tick, so the human turns at the end of tick T+29 and an exposed human is healthy again at the end of tick T+1. A human that first sees a zombie mid-tick uses the stance rolled at the previous tick end.

rules.name: compatibility
rules.text: a = aggression/100, i = (intelligence - 1)/9. d = w_a*|a1 - a2| + w_i*|i1 - i2|. compat = clip(1 - compat_slope * d, -1, 1). Symmetric and deterministic.

rules.name: likeability update
rules.text: After R10, once per tick, on positions after the 10th step, for each living healthy or exposed human H and for each direction H->P independently. Take the snapshot of H's held and pending values. For every living healthy or exposed human P within the bond radius: v = clip(v_old + like_rate*compat(H,P), -1, 1), where v_old is the held value, else the pending value, else 0. For every held or pending P outside the bond radius: v = v_old*(1 - like_decay). Drop |v| < prune_below. Rank and keep the top 5 as in relations.Likes.capacity_rule. Sleeping humans update. The baseline arm runs R8 identically; only R9 is disabled.

rules.name: social pull
rules.text: Evaluated every step for an awake living human H with no living zombie within the perception radius (checked every step, not only at tick end). Candidates are held partners P that are alive, state healthy or exposed (infected friends are not candidates, author decision), within the perception radius, with L >= pull_threshold. The target is the candidate with the highest L, ties to the lower agent_id. If the target is farther than stop_distance, H moves toward it at speed*dt; if at or within stop_distance, H does not move. With no candidate, H wanders (R11). Rivals (L <= -pull_threshold) have no behaviour. Disabled in the baseline arm. Known limitation: R9 does not check that the partner is safe.

rules.name: relationship end
rules.text: At the end of each tick, after R6 and before R8: remove every agent that is dead, infected or has turned from all slots and pending tables, and clear its own. Deaths and bites between purges are handled by R9, which ignores partners that are not living healthy or exposed humans at the moment of the decision. The constraint 'no relationship with a dead, infected or zombie agent' holds at tick boundaries.

rules.name: wander
rules.text: A living agent with no target (a zombie with no human in sight; a human with no zombie in sight and no R9 target) does heading += uniform(-turn_rate, turn_rate)*dt and then moves speed*dt along the heading, every step. Positions are clamped to the map after moving; heading is not changed by the clamp.

tick_schedule: every step (10 per tick), from step-start positions: decide for all agents (R1, R2, R3, R9, R11); then move everyone and clamp to the map; then contact damage (R4), simultaneous
after the 10th step: tick += 1; bites (R5); infection and exposure timers and turning (R6); R10; R8; stance roll (R3) for all living humans, including at night; sample metrics
constraints: agent_id values are unique whole numbers
life_value <= 0 if and only if state is dead
every numeric attribute lies inside its valid range
every agent is inside the map
human state is one of healthy, exposed, infected, dead; zombie state is one of turned, dead
a human holds at most 5 relationships, none with itself, none with a zombie, an infected or a dead agent (at tick boundaries)
conversion keeps agent_id; ids are never reused

metrics.humans_alive: living humans with state healthy, exposed or infected per tick (matches zombie_storage.py:179-180)
metrics.humans_infected: count of infected humans per tick
metrics.survival_rate: humans_alive at each checkpoint tick / 750; also report humans_not_infected at the same ticks (both reported, engine count is the headline)
metrics.time_to_extinction: first tick with zero living humans, or null if capped
metrics.lost_member: a human is lost if it is dead or has turned
metrics.spatial_cluster: connected components of living humans with pairwise distance <= bond radius, sampled at cluster_sample_tick; independent of L; singletons excluded
metrics.cluster_count_and_size: L-based components with L >= cluster_threshold among living healthy or exposed humans, singletons excluded, sampled at cluster_sample_tick and also reported at ticks 30 and 100. Interpret only relative to baseline and to the spatial metric: L-defined clusters have lower aggression variance by construction
metrics.aggression_homophily: pooled within-cluster aggression variance (clusters of size >= 2) / variance over all living humans at the sample time; computed for both spatial and L-based clusters
metrics.fighter_vs_runner_bands: mean aggression per cluster at cluster_sample_tick vs fraction of its members lost within outcome_window ticks
metrics.sampling_point: end of tick after R8 at tick % 10 == 0 (the start of a day), identical in both arms

baseline.note: same ontology and code; likeability tracked (R8) but R9 disabled

experiments.run_length: until no living humans remain (author decision), with safety_cap_ticks as an engineering guard
experiments.execution: one run at a time, arms run sequentially (author decision)
experiments.pairing: seed k is used in both arms; initial population (positions, attributes, headings) comes from rng_init(seed), dynamics from a separate rng_dyn(seed, arm). Both arms start from the same population.
experiments.reporting: per-seed paired differences in survival_rate, time_to_extinction, spatial and L-based homophily, with mean and a 95% interval

rule_in_order.note: marks 'intelligence above 5' only, no lab in this version
10 is the midpoint of the 5-15 starting range

rule_in_order.if: any other human with an odd agent_id
any other human with an even agent_id

relationship_listing.contents: up to 5 partners: agent id, likeability, partner aggression and intelligence

references.title: Mesa 3: Agent-based modeling with Python in 2025

known_limitations: no shuffled-pull control arm (pull toward random humans): an effect could come from clumping rather than similarity
R9 does not check partner safety, so oscillation near fights is possible
with stop distance 20, several friends can still touch the same zombie
exposed is almost cosmetic: bites treat exposed and healthy alike
wander is nearly straight (persistence about 667 units on a 1451 map) and agents slide along walls
R9 is dormant until about tick 20-30 because zombies are within sight of almost everyone
metrics sampled at tick % 10 == 0 are phase-locked to the start of a day
coordinator's supporting numbers came from a rough re-implementation with 3-4 seeds, indicative only
implementation_notes: Model.step = one sub-step; a tick counter increments after every 10 steps.
One agent class with a mutable kind; do not recreate agents on turning.

Use Mesa 3.5.x and record which continuous-space class is used. The legacy mesa.space.ContinuousSpace raises if x >= side or < 0 (tested in 3.5.3); clamp to [0, side) before every move. The engine clamps inclusively (simulation.py:574-575), so this is a deliberate one-ulp difference.
Two-pass update: decide for all agents from step-start positions, then move all. Activation order is then irrelevant.
Build one spatial index per step; do not call a per-agent neighbour query.
Line numbers cited were verified against the MAOO3 copy.
